chapter: Chicago's South Side night life in the early 1920s
title: Why Chicago led New York in cabarets and night life
summary: Chicago was the cabaret center of the country around 1922, with a concentrated black population.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: No, didn't do any harm. No, because it's so -- of course, Chicago was so far ahead of New York at that time for night life because every corner you had a club, after hour joints, you know. Like, for instance—
Well, why was that?
Why was Chicago ahead of New York?
Well, at that particular time Chicago was cabaret center in this country because you --
(Side Ten)
Well, what we're really talking about here is Chicago, which was kind of unique, but the night life thing in Chicago in the South Side when you left in '24 -- is that right --
Yeah.
-- was far ahead of Harlem.
That's right.
Well now, what we're trying to do is account for why this was.
Well, first place --
Just excuse me for one second, Happy. Was there a bigger black population in Chicago then than in New York?
I think for night life, yes, it was, because --
I mean in total.
In total population you mean.
Well, I mean was the black population in Chicago bigger than New York?
I think so, particular time. I think so.
Yeah. Or maybe more concentrated.

Yeah, it was more concentrated, because most of it be outside of downtown, like the West Side in Chicago. Well, that was a different thing because they had a lot of smaller clubs over there. I used to go over there and work sometime. But like the big clubs like Sunset, Entertainers, Dreamland and Auto Cafe, the Rime Cafe and like -- them type of clubs was all concentrated.
